title: Topology Resonance Kernel Prober: topology-aware seqlen probing and resonance-based kernel scoring
creator: Liam O'Neill
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, online probing component that computes a topology-aware 'resonance' score for candidate attention/matrix-multiply microkernels given observed request sequence-length distributions and node topology. Motivation: current kernel choice heuristics rely on static cost tables or coarse seqlen buckets and miss regime shifts from mixed workloads (short chat turns vs. long document generation) and topology effects (NUMA/GPU-interconnect). The Resonance Prober will enable lower-latency choices for prefills and decodes while preserving throughput and guardrails for tail latency.

Scope and approach:
- Offline microbench: extended microbenchmark harness to run short (<50ms) experiments across microkernels on representative hardware topologies (single GPU, NVLink pair, PCIe host). Capture occupancy, bandwidth, kernel runtime variance as function of seqlen and kv-cache size.
- Online seqlen probe: lightweight sampler embedded in runtime that maintains a short rolling seqlen histogram (per-route and global), then triggers microprobes when drift is detected. Microprobes are non-blocking and run on low-priority worker threads; results feed resonance scoring.
- Resonance score: composite metric combining predicted latency, throughput, occupancy headroom, and stability (variance). Includes topology-adaptive terms for cross-GPU bandwidth sensitivity. Score is normalized to allow comparisons across model variants and quantized kernels.
- Decision policy: pick kernel with highest resonance score subject to safety margin constraints. If predicted P99 exceeds route SLO or probe confidence low, fallback to conservative kernel and schedule reprobing.
- Prefill vs decode scheduling: treat prefill microbench differently (larger batch occupancy, KV warmstart) versus decode microbench (many short calls). Policy will prefer kernels optimized for batching on prefill paths and low-latency variant for decode.
- Telemetry and evals: emit per-decision telemetry (resonance_score, probe_age, kernel_choice, latency p50/p95/p99) to console. Build evaluation dashboards and offline regression tests using existing eval harness.

Success criteria:
- 5-10% median latency improvement on mixed workloads in dev cluster without increasing P99 beyond 2% over baseline.
- No customer-visible regressions during canary; rollbacks automated on >5% P99 spike.
- Safe fallbacks enabled for nodes with low probe coverage.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement cross-region routing or dedicated capacity admission control. It focuses on per-node/cluster kernel choices and local topology awareness.
